newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel wants broker fees liberalised in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel wants broker fees liberalised in 1999.

text.p: A key advisory panel to Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) has reached a basic agreement to recommend that brokerage commissions be fully deregulated by the end of 1999, panel sources told Reuters on Tuesday.
As a stop-gap measure until fees are fully deregulated, the Securities and Exchange Council agreed to propose liberalising commissions on stock transactions of more than 50 million yen in April 1998.
At present, there are no restrictions on commissions for transactions of more than one billion yen.
The panel, which is advising the finance minister on "Big Bang" market reforms, will submit its final report on Friday.
The council will also suggest replacing the current licensing system of securities firms with a new registration system during the year to March 1999, the sources said.

All existing brokerages are expected to be given permission to register, although some panel members have pointed out the need for setting up a certain criteria to check new-comers to the securities business, the sources said.
The panel's final recommendation would also include the removal of a rule barring banks' securities units from certain areas of equities-related operations after September 1997.

The panel will also propose that the fire-wall between operations of brokerages and bank-affiliated brokerages be fully abolished after September 1999, the sources said. -- Yoko Matsudaira, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-5473-3705
